issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 5.3 (and downstream Theorem 5.10) asserts exponential convergence of the reconstructed fields to the physical outgoing solution $u$ in $H^1(K)$ for every compact $K \Subset \Omega_R$. However, $\Omega_R = \Omega_p \cup P$ contains the absorbing PML layer $P$. Inside $P$, coordinate stretching is active: the numerical fields $u_\sigma^{\rm ni}$ and $u_\sigma^c$ are exponentially decaying in $\bar\sigma$, whereas the physical solution $u$ is unstretched, radiating, and generally non-zero. Hence $\|u - u_\sigma\|_{H^1(K)}$ cannot converge to zero when $K$ intersects the PML region. The underlying PML-PDE convergence result (Theorem 3.4, eq. (3.8)) and Theorem 4.3 only hold for $K \Subset \Omega_p$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Theorem 5.3 and Theorem 5.10 by replacing $K \Subset \Omega_R$ with $K \Subset \Omega_p$, matching the hypotheses of Theorem 3.4 and Theorem 4.3.
issues.overall_effect: The compact-field convergence bounds in Theorem 5.3 (eq. (5.27)) and Theorem 5.10 (eq. (5.43)) fail when $K$ intersects the PML region $\Omega_R \setminus \overline{\Omega_p}$. Valid convergence to the true wave field $u$ is restricted to compact subsets of the physical domain $\Omega_p$.
issues.title: Compact field convergence claimed on entire truncated domain instead of physical region
issues.why_classification: Restricting $K$ to compact subsets of $\Omega_p$ is a routine, local correction that preserves all substantive methodology, convergence rates, and the paper's advertised scope (which explicitly states convergence in the physical region $\Omega_p$).
